## Details on Broadcasted Operators {.unnumbered}


### Description

Base 'R' comes with relational,
arithmetic, integer, logical, and bit-wise operators. <br>
'broadcast' provides 2 ways to use these operators with broadcasting. <br>
<br>
The first (and simple) way is to use the [broadcaster](broadcaster.qmd) class,
which comes with it's own method dispatch for the above mentioned operators. <br>
This approach supports operator precedence, and for the average 'R' user,
this is sufficient. <br>
<br>
The second way is to use the large set of <code>bc.</code>- functions. <br>
These offer much greater control and more operators than the previous method,
and has less risk of running into conflicting methods. <br>
But they do not support operator precedence. <br>
<br>



### Operators Overloaded via Broadcaster Class

The 'broadcast' package provides the [broadcaster](broadcaster.qmd) class,
which comes with its own method dispatch for the base operators. <br>
If at least one of the 2 arguments of the base operators has the [broadcaster](broadcaster.qmd) class attribute,
and no other class (like <code>bit64</code>) interferes,
broadcasting will be used. <br>
<br>
The following operators have a 'broadcaster' method:

<div class="sourceCode r"><pre># relational operators       : ==, !=, &lt;, &gt;, &lt;=, &gt;=
# arithmetic operators       : +, -, *, /, ^,
# integer operators          : %%, %/%
# logical operators          : &amp;, |
# bit-wise operators         : &amp;, | (both sides type of `raw`)

</pre></div>
See also the Examples section below. <br>
Unary operations (i.e. <code>+ x</code>, <code>- x</code>) return the original object,
with only the sign adjusted. <br>
<br>



### Available <code>bc.</code> functions

'broadcast' provides a set of functions for broadcasted element-wise binary operations
with broadcasting. <br>
These functions use an API similar to the outer function. <br>
<br>
The following functions for simple operations are available:


<ul>
<li> [bc.rel](bc.rel.qmd): General relational operations
(<code style="white-space: pre;">==, !=, &lt;, &gt;, &lt;=, &gt;=</code>). <br>
The various other <code>bc.</code> methods below have specialised relational operators available for specialised needs.

</li>
<li> [bc.b](bc.b.qmd): Boolean/logical operations;

</li>
<li> [bc.i](bc.i.qmd): integer operations;

</li>
<li> [bc.d](bc.d.qmd): decimal arithmetic operations;

</li>
<li> [bc.cplx](bc.cplx.qmd): complex arithmetic operations;

</li>
<li> [bc.str](bc.str.qmd): string (in)equality, concatenation, and distance operations;

</li>
<li> [bc.raw](bc.raw.qmd): operations that take in arrays of type <code>raw</code> and return an array of type <code>raw</code>;

</li>
<li> [bc.bit](bc.bit.qmd): BIT-WISE operations, supporting the <code>raw</code> and <code>integer</code> types;

</li>
<li> [bc.list](bc.list.qmd): apply any 'R' function to 2 recursive arrays with broadcasting. <br> <br>

</li></ul>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>"}
library("broadcast")


# maths ====

x <- 1:10
y <- 1:10
dim(x) <- c(10, 1)
dim(y) <- c(1, 10)
broadcaster(x) <- TRUE
broadcaster(y) <- TRUE



x + y / x
(x + y) / x

(x + y) * x


# relational operators ====
x <- 1:10
y <- array(1:10, c(1, 10))
broadcaster(x) <- TRUE
broadcaster(y) <- TRUE

x == y
x != y
x < y
x > y
x <= y
x >= y




# maths ====

x <- sample(1:10)
y <- sample(1:10)
dim(x) <- c(10, 1)
dim(y) <- c(1, 10)
mbroadcasters(c("x", "y"), TRUE)



x + y / x
(x + y) / x

(x + y) * x


# relational operators ====
x <- 1:10
y <- array(1:10, c(1, 10))
mbroadcasters(c("x", "y"), TRUE)

x == y
x != y
x < y
x > y
x <= y
x >= y




```
